{{Short description|French pair skater (born 1994)}} {{Infobox figure skater | name = Camille Kovalev | image = Camille Kovalev & Pavel Kovalev 2025 Worlds Short Program 00.jpg | image_size = 250px | caption = Camille and Pavel Kovalev at the [[2025 World Figure Skating Championships|2025 World Championships]] | full_name = | other_names = Camille Mendoza | country = {{FRA}} | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1994|11|29|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Toulouse, France]] | hometown = [[Angers, France]] | height = 1.60 m | partner = [[Pavel Kovalev (figure skater)|Pavel Kovalev]] (since 2014)
[[Christopher Boyadji]]
(2011–12) | coach = [[Bruno Massot]] | skating_club = Club Olympique de Courbevoie | began_skating = 2000 | retired = | medal_record = {{Figure skating infobox medals|nationals=French |NC={{FS medal|g|NC|nationals=French|2022|Cergy-Pontoise|p}}{{FS medal|g|NC|nationals=French|2023|Rouen|p}}{{FS medal|g|NC|nationals=French|2024|Vaujany|p}}{{FS medal|g|NC|nationals=French|2025|Annecy|p}}{{FS medal|g|NC|nationals=French|2026|Briancon|p}}{{FS medal|s|NC|nationals=French|2016|Épinal|p}}{{FS medal|s|NC|nationals=French|2020|Dunkirk|p}}{{FS medal|b|NC|nationals=French|2017|Caen|p}}{{FS medal|b|NC|nationals=French|2019|Vaujany|p}} }} | discipline = [[Pair skating]] }} '''Camille Kovalev''' ([[née]] '''Mendoza'''; born 29 November 1994 in [[Toulouse]]) is a French [[pair skater]]. With [[Pavel Kovalev (figure skater)|Pavel Kovalev]], she is a two-time [[ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|ISU Grand Prix]] medalist, 2018 [[Volvo Open Cup]] silver medalist, 2015 [[International Cup of Nice]] bronze medalist, 2015 [[Lombardia Trophy]] bronze medalist, and is a five-time [[French Figure Skating Championships|French national champion]] (2022–26). Earlier in her career, she skated with [[Christopher Boyadji]] and competed in the final segment at the [[2012 World Junior Figure Skating Championships|2012 World Junior Championships]]. == Personal life == Kovalev was born on 29 November 1994 in [[Toulouse]], [[France]]. She married her skating partner, [[Pavel Kovalev (figure skater)|Pavel Kovalev]], in December 2017 and subsequently adopted his last name. == Career == === Early career === [[File:2012 World Junior FS Camille Mendoza Christopher Boyadji.jpg|left|thumb|Camille Kovalev and Christopher Boyadji at the [[2012 World Junior Figure Skating Championships|2012 World Junior Championships]]]] Kovalev began figure skating in 2000 at the age of six. She began competing as a pair skater in 2011 after teaming up with [[Christopher Boyadji]]. Coached by Vivien Rolland and Diana Skotnicka, Kovalev/Boyadji represented the Club Olympique de Courbevoie. They competed at the [[2012 World Junior Figure Skating Championships|2012 World Junior Championships]], where they finished sixteenth. Their partnership eventually dissolved following the [[2011–12 figure skating season]]. === Pair skating with Pavel Kovalev === ==== 2014–2015 season: Debut of Kovalev/Kovalev ==== In 2014, it was announced that Kovalev had teamed up with Russian pair skater, [[Pavel Kovalev (figure skater)|Pavel Kovalev]] and that they would be coached by [[Medhi Bouzzine]] and that they would represent the Club Olympique de Courbevoie.{{cite web |title=Camille MENDOZA / Pavel KOVALEV: 2015/2016 |url=http://isuresults.com/bios/isufs00034726.htm |website=International Skating Union |publisher=International Skating Union |access-date=2 November 2024 |archive-date=25 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225122712/http://isuresults.com/bios/isufs00034726.htm |url-status=bot: unknown }} Their first competition as a team was at the [[Master's de Patinage|2014 Master's de Patinage]], although they withdrew from the event after placing third in the short program. They subsequently competed at the [[NRW Trophy|2014 NRW Trophy]] and the [[Bavarian Open|2015 Bavarian Open]], finishing fourth at both events. ==== 2015–2016 season ==== The Kovalevs started the season by winning their first international medal together, a bronze at the [[Lombardia Trophy|2015 Lombardia Trophy]]. They then went on to win silver at the [[Master's de Patinage|2015 Master's de Patinage]] and bronze at the [[Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur|2015 Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur]]. In December, the Kovalevs won silver at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2016 French Championships]]. They then closed the season with a fourth-place finish at the [[Bavarian Open|2016 Bavarian Open]]. ==== 2016–2017 season ==== Beginning the season with a gold medal win at the [[Master's de Patinage|2016 Master's de Patinage]], the Kovalevs subsequently finished sixth at the [[Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur|2016 Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur]] and fourth at the [[2016 CS Tallinn Trophy]]. They ended the season by winning bronze at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2017 French Championships]]. ==== 2017–2018 season ==== The Kovalevs started the season by winning bronze at the [[Master's de Patinage|2017 Master's de Patinage]]. They then competed at the [[Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur|2017 Trophée Métropole Nice Côte d'Azur]] and the [[2017 CS Tallinn Trophy]], finishing eighth and fifth, respectively. ==== 2018–2019 season ==== The Kovalevs began the season by winning silver at the [[Master's de Patinage|2018 Master's de Patinage]] and at the [[Volvo Open Cup|2018 Volvo Open Cup]]. They then concluded the season by winning bronze at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2019 French Championships]]. ==== 2019–2020 season ==== Beginning the season at the [[Master's de Patinage|2020 Master's de Patinage]], the Kovalevs won the gold medal. They then went on to compete on the [[2019–20 ISU Challenger Series]], finishing thirteenth at the [[2019 CS Warsaw Cup]] and seventeenth at the [[2019 CS Golden Spin of Zagreb]]. In December, the Kovalevs won their second national silver medal at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2020 French Championships]]. ==== 2020–2021 season ==== The Kovalevs only competed at one event in the 2020-2021 season, the [[Master's de Patinage|2020 Master's de Patinage]], where they won the bronze medal. ==== 2021–2022 season: First national title and World Championship debut ==== In fall 2021, it was announced that the Kovalevs were now being coached by [[Laurent Depouilly]] in [[Courbevoie]]. They started the season by finishing seventh at the [[2021 CS Lombardia Trophy]]. Making their [[2021–22 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|Grand Prix]] series debut at the [[2021 Internationaux de France]], the pair came in seventh place. In December, they won their first national title at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2022 French Championships]]. With this result, the Kovalevs were selected to represent France at the European and World Championships for a first time. At the [[2022 European Figure Skating Championships|2022 European Championships]] in [[Tallinn]], Estonia, they came in fourteenth place. In March 2022, the [[International Skating Union]] banned athletes representing Russia from competing at international events as a result of their [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|invasion of Ukraine]]. In addition, the [[Chinese Skating Association]] opted not to send any athletes to compete at the [[2022 World Figure Skating Championships|2022 World Championships]] in [[Montpellier]], France.{{cite news |url= https://www.cbc.ca/sports/the-buzzer-figure-skating-world-championships-preview-1.6393780 |title= Get ready for a bizarre figure skating world championships |work= [[CBC Sports]] |last= Campigotto |first= Jesse |date= March 22, 2022 }} Because of this, the Kovalevs finished World Championships with a strong eighth-place. ==== 2022–2023 season: First Grand Prix medal ==== The Kovalevs began the season by finishing sixth at the [[2022 CS Nebelhorn Trophy]] before going on to win gold at the [[Master's de Patinage|2022 Master's de Patinage]]. Going on to compete on the [[2022–23 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|2022–23 Grand Prix]] circuit, the pair won their first Grand Prix medal, a silver, at the [[2022 Grand Prix de France]]. They subsequently finished fifth at the [[2022 NHK Trophy]]. In December, the Kovalevs won the national title for a second consecutive time at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2023 French Championships]]. Named to the European and World team, the Kovalevs finished sixth at the [[2023 European Figure Skating Championships|2023 European Championships]] in [[Espoo]], Finland and fourteenth at the [[2023 World Figure Skating Championships|2023 World Championships]] in [[Saitama (city)|Saitama]], Japan. Selected to compete for Team France in the pairs discipline at the [[2023 ISU World Team Trophy in Figure Skating|2023 World Team Trophy]], the pair individually placed fifth and Team France finished in fifth place overall. ==== 2023–2024 season: Second Grand Prix medal ==== The Kovalevs started the season by winning gold at the [[John Nicks Pairs Challenge|2023 John Nicks Pairs Challenge]]. Following a ninth-place finish at the [[2023 CS Autumn Classic International]], the pair won gold for a fourth time at the [[Master's de Patinage|2023 Master's de Patinage]]. They subsequently competed at the [[2023 CS Finlandia Trophy]], where they placed fifth. Competing on the [[2023–24 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|2023–24 Grand Prix]] circuit, the Kovalevs won the bronze medal at the [[2023 Grand Prix de France]]. “We are so happy,” said Camille. “We came here with the goal to win a medal and we did it. We fought until the end to get it!” They went on to finish fifth at the [[2023 Grand Prix of Espoo]]. In December, they won their third national title at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2024 French Championships]]. The pair then went on to compete at the [[2024 European Figure Skating Championships|2024 European Championships]] in [[Kaunas, Lithuania]], despite Camille developing a fever two days before the event. During the short program, Camille had a very hard fall on the throw triple flip, landing on her chest. She then fell again on the side-by-side triple toe. As a result of these mistakes, the pair only placed fifteenth in the short program. They ended up withdrawing before the free skate due to Camille's illness.{{cite web |title=LIVE - Pairs Short Program - ISU European Championships - Kaunas 2024 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WCG_GDCneDQ&t=9919s |website=YouTube |publisher=YouTube |access-date=2 November 2024}}{{cite web |title=Pour préserver l'intégrité physique de Camille, malade, elle et son mari Pavel Kovalev ont déclaré forfait pour le programme libre de ce jeudi. |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Patinage-artistique/Actualites/Camille-et-pavel-kovalev-declarent-forfait-t-pour-le-programme-libre-des-couples/1441524 |website=Lequipe |publisher=Lequipe |access-date=2 November 2024}} The Kovalevs subsequently competed at the [[International Challenge Cup|2024 International Challenge Cup]], where they took the bronze medal. Weeks before the [[2024 World Figure Skating Championships|2024 World Championships]], the Kovalevs announced that they would not compete at the event due to Pavel injuring himself from a very bad fall in training.{{cite web |last1=Kovalev |first1=Camille |title=Juste une petite annonce, pas la plus agréable à faire mais importante... |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C35vvKKLuv7/ |website=Instagram |publisher=Instagram |access-date=2 November 2024}} In June, the pair announced that while continuing their coaching relationship with [[Laurent Depouilly]], that they would begin training at the ASGA Figure Skating Club.{{cite web |last1=Kovalev |first1=Camille |title=On vous annonce officiellement qu'on a décidé de rejoindre le club @asgapatinageartistique pour les saisons à venir. |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C79b8o_IXsv/ |website=Instagram |publisher=Instagram |access-date=2 November 2024}} ==== 2024–2025 season ==== [[File:Camille Kovalev & Pavel Kovalev 2025 Worlds Short Program 01.jpg|thumb|321x321px|The Kovalev's at the [[2025 World Figure Skating Championships|2025 World Championships]]]] During the off-season, Pavel dislocated his ankle and underwent surgery during the summer. He also injured his back shortly after returning to the ice, and would subsequently be forced to miss another two weeks of training. The Kovalevs, having initially been told by doctors that they would likely need to sit out of the beginning of the season, Pavel was eventually cleared to skate at the [[Master's de Patinage|2024 Master's de Patinage]] in late September, much earlier than the couple had expected. They ultimately won silver at the event.{{cite web |last1=Mathieu |first1=Solène |title=Interview Camille et Pavel Kovalev, Laurent Depouilly : cap vers Angers pour l'objectif JO |url=https://www.skate-info-glace.com/kovalevdepouilly0924/ |website=Skate-Info |publisher=Skate-Info |access-date=2 November 2024}}{{cite web |last1=Kovalev |first1=Camille |title=Fin des Masters 2024, Nous étions présent pour avancer dans notre préparation en vue des Grands Prix. |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DAg9iQ6IkL1/ |website=Instagram |publisher=Instagram |access-date=2 November 2024}} They subsequently finished sixth at the [[Tayside Trophy|2024 Tayside Trophy]]. Going on to compete on the [[2024–25 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|2024–25 Grand Prix]] circuit, the Kovalevs finished seventh at the [[2024 Grand Prix de France]] and sixth at the [[2024 Cup of China]]. In late December, the Kovalevs won their fourth national title at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2025 French Championships]]. The Kovalevs then competed at the [[2025 European Figure Skating Championships|2025 European Championships]] in [[Tallinn]], Estonia, where they finished ninth overall. They subsequently finished fourth at the Road to 26 Trophy in [[Milan]], Italy, a test event for the [[2026 Winter Olympics]]. Selected to compete at the [[2025 World Figure Skating Championships|2025 World Championships]] in [[Boston, Massachusetts]], United States, the Kovalevs placed twenty-first in the short program and did not advance to the free skate segment. They then closed the season by competing for Team France at the [[2025 ISU World Team Trophy in Figure Skating|2025 World Team Trophy]], placing sixth in all segments of the pairs event and Team France finished fourth overall. ==== 2025–2026 season: Milano Cortina Olympics ==== [[File:Camille Kovalev and Pavel Kovalev at Pairs Free Skating at 2026 ISU World Figure Skating Championships Prague 07 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Kovalev's performing at the [[2026 World Figure Skating Championships|2026 World Championships]]]] In June, the Kovalevs announced that they had made a coaching change from [[Laurent Depouilly]] to [[Bruno Massot]].{{cite web |title=✨ Nouveau coach ✨ |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DKzzVHEso7N/?hl=en |website=Instagram |publisher=Instagram |access-date=12 June 2025}} They opened the season by winning gold at the [[Master's de Patinage|2025 Master's de Patinage]]. They then competed at the [[ISU Skate to Milano|2025 Skate to Milano]], the final Olympic qualifying event. At the event, the Kovalevs placed second in the short program and fifth in the free skate, placing fourth overall. Due to this placement, Team France was given the first alternate spot for pair skating at the [[2026 Winter Olympics]].{{cite web |title=Communication No. 2741 - OLYMPIC WINTER GAMES 2026 ENTRIES/PARTICIPATION SINGLE & PAIR SKATING AND ICE DANCE |url=https://isu-d8g8b4b7ece7aphs.a03.azurefd.net/isudamcontainer/CMS/Corporate-Site/Governance/Transparency/ISU-Communications/2741-OWG-Figure-Skating-Qualification-Competition-and-Judges-Draw-Beijing-1758706754-2014.pdf |website=International Skating Union |publisher=International Skating Union |access-date=2 January 2026}} Going on to compete on the [[2025–26 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating|2025–26 Grand Prix]] series, the Kovalevs finished sixth at the [[2025 Grand Prix de France]]. They went on to compete at the [[2025 NHK Trophy]], however, Camille sustained a shoulder injury following a fall on their side-by-side triple toe attempt in the short program. As a result, the team was forced to withdraw. According to their coach, Bruno Massot, the injury involved a dislocation, but the available three-minute injury recovery period was insufficient for her to resume skating. Kovalev did not require immediate hospital treatment and was expected to undergo further evaluation upon returning home. In December, the Kovalevs competed at the [[French Figure Skating Championships|2026 French Championships]], where they won their fifth national title. They were subsequently named to the [[2026 Winter Olympics|2026 Winter Olympic]] team to compete in the figure skating team event.{{cite web |title=🚨 SÉLECTION OFFICIELLE 🚨 𝗘𝗻 𝗿𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗠𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗻-𝗖𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗮 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DSm4CagCGct/ |website=Instagram |publisher=Equipe de France |access-date=1 January 2026}} The following month, the Kovalevs competed at the [[2026 European Figure Skating Championships|2026 European Championships]] in [[Sheffield, England]], United Kingdom, where they finished in tenth place. Less than two weeks before the start of the 2026 Winter Olympics, it was announced that the Winter Sports Association of Uzbekistan had reliquinshed their sole Olympic pair skating spot. As the first alternates, the Kovalevs were selected to compete in the Games' individual pair event.{{cite web |last1=Penicaud |first1=Céline |title=JO de Milano Cortina 2026 : Camille et Pavel Kovalev participeront aussi à l'épreuve de couples en patinage artistique |url=https://www.olympics.com/fr/milano-cortina-2026/actualite/milano-cortina-2026-camille-pavel-kovalev-participeront-epreuve-couples-patinage-artistique |website=Olympics.com |publisher=Olympics.com |access-date=29 January 2026}} On February 6, the Kovalevs placed seventh in the short program in the [[Figure skating at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Team event|2026 Winter Olympics Figure Skating Team Event]]. [https://www.goldenskate.com/author/paulaslater/ Paula Slater] says, “There’s so much to enjoy here,” said Camille. “Honestly, everything. It feels like a dream come true. Every moment, we try to take pictures, look around, see what’s happening next, what we can do next. I really feel like a kid in Disneyland!”{{cite news |url=https://www.goldenskate.com/miura-and-kihara-deliver-crucial-boost-for-japan-in-pairs-olympic-team-event/ |title=Miura and Kihara deliver crucial boost for Japan in Pairs Olympic Team event |first=Paula |last=Slater |work=Golden Skate |date=February 6, 2026}} ==== 2026–2027 season ==== The pair opened their season with a 6th place finish at the [[2026 CS Kinoshita Group Cup|2026 Kinoshita Group Cup]].{{Cite web |title=ISU CS Kinoshita Group Cup 2026 - Pairs |url=https://www.jsfresults.com/InterNational/2026-2027/csjpn2026/CAT003RS.htm |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=www.jsfresults.com}} == Programs == === With Pavel Kovalev === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! (born December 1, 1988) is an American [[Gridiron football|football]] coach and former player who is currently the [[head coach]] at [[Texas State University]]. He played as a [[quarterback]] and was signed by the [[New York Jets]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2012. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]]. ==Early years== Kinne was born in [[Mesquite, Texas]], a suburb just east of [[Dallas]], to Gary Joe Kinne and Jocelyne Karr. His father was a former standout linebacker at [[Baylor University]] and later an assistant coach at [[Allen High School (Allen, Texas)|Allen High School]], [[Kaufman High School]], and was the defensive coordinator at [[Mesquite High School (Mesquite, Texas)|Mesquite High School]], along with eventually being the head coach of [[Sherman High School (Texas)|Sherman High School]]. In 2003, his father accepted the head coaching job at [[Canton High School (Texas)|Canton High School]] in [[East Texas]], a town about 60 miles east of Dallas. Kinne became the starting quarterback of the Eagle varsity football team as a freshman. In his first game against rival [[Grand Saline High School]], Kinne played well and exhibited a strong arm and good accuracy despite a 20–13 loss. He led Canton High to its first playoff victory since 1964 and finished the year as Class AAA area finalists with an 8–4 record. He was named ''All East Texas'' and was named ''The Tyler Morning Telegraph'''s East Texas Newcomer of the year. As a sophomore, he led CHS to another good season with an 8–2 record but narrowly missed the playoffs. === Father's shooting === In the spring of 2005, Kinne's father, who was also his coach at Canton High, was shot in the chest by the disgruntled parent of one of the players he coached. According to police reports, Jeff Doyal Robertson, the father of a player who had often complained to coaches and administrators regarding the way his son was treated, walked into the Canton Fieldhouse and shot Coach Kinne at point blank range. Robertson then fled in his pickup truck and headed east towards [[Tyler, Texas]]. Kinne Sr. was on the phone with another coach who was at another school when he was shot. Kinne Jr. was taken by police into protective custody, and then told that his father had died when in fact he had survived despite being given only a 10% chance to live.{{cite news |url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/TU/article.aspx?subjectid=94&articleid=20090805_94_b1_jamesg157451 |title=Shot of reality: Attack on father makes TU QB mentally tough |author=Eric Bailey |date=August 5, 2009 |newspaper=Tulsa World}}{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/g-j-kinne-comes-to-jets-with-incredible-backstory-09000d5d828c9725 |title=G.J. Kinne comes to Jets with incredible backstory |publisher=NFL |work=[[NFL.com]] |author=Dan Hanzus |date=May 1, 2012}} Robertson was later apprehended in an area north of Tyler near [[Interstate 20]] where he had slashed his wrists in an apparent [[suicide attempt]]. Robertson was convicted of [[aggravated assault]] with a deadly weapon and was sentenced to 20 years in prison.[https://www.kltv.com/story/4572666/robertson-gets-maximum-sentence/ Robertson Gets Maximum Sentence – KLTV] ===Senior year=== After the shooting, Kinne stayed one more year at Canton High School, leading the team to its best season in school history with a 12–2 record, losing to [[Tatum High School]], the eventual state champion. After the 2005 season, Kinne's father, who had recovered from his wounds, was offered a job at [[Baylor University]], which he accepted. Kinne then decided to move to [[Gilmer, Texas]] about 70 miles to the east of Canton, to live with his mother and stepfather. The decision to move was controversial as many speculated that Kinne moved for athletic reasons, which is prohibited by the UIL, the governing body of Texas high school athletics. Kinne enrolled at Gilmer High School and became the starting quarterback, leading the Buckeyes to a 10–0 record, but was upset in the first round of the playoffs by Liberty-Eylau High School. He finished his career with 11,695 passing yards and 130 [[touchdown]] passes. He also rushed for 3,327 yards with 48 touchdowns. {{College athlete recruit start|40=yes|collapse=no|year=2007}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = G.J. Kinne Profile |publisher=MSN |work=www.scout.com |accessdate=December 21, 2012}} ==College career== Kinne attended the [[University of Texas at Austin]] as a redshirt freshman in 2007, but was buried in the depth chart and decided to transfer. He transferred to the [[University of Tulsa]] effective May 7, 2008.{{Cite web |date=2008-05-07 |title=Texas backup QB Kinne is transferring to Tulsa |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=3385926 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} Kinne became the starting quarterback for the Golden Hurricane in 2009 and remained the starter throughout his career. Recruited under coach [[Gus Malzahn]], he finished his career with 9,472 yards and 81 touchdowns. In 2010 he was named C-USA Offensive Player of the Year and First-team All-C-USA as he led the team to a Conference-USA co-championship, a victory over #24 Hawaii in the [[2010 Hawaii Bowl]] and a final ranking of #24. In 2011 he led them to an 8-3 regular season record and a trip to the [[2011 Armed Forces Bowl]] which they lost in the last 11 seconds to BYU; and he was named to the C-USA second team. squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 9, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910134125/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-sign-LB-Jasper-Brinkley-add-2-to-practice-squad/b901f374-e2e1-431d-a5f4-c223cfcb1d2f |archive-date=September 10, 2015 |url-status=dead }} On September 16, 2015, he was released by the Giants.{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-three-players-to-practice-squad/284c2bec-a9bf-4d12-825e-335fbe01cf35 |title=Giants add three players to practice squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 16, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926091932/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-three-players-to-practice-squad/284c2bec-a9bf-4d12-825e-335fbe01cf35 |archive-date=September 26, 2015 |url-status=dead }} On September 30, 2015, he was re-signed to the Giants' practice squad.{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-WR-Tavarres-King-QB-GJ-Kinne-to-practice-squad/46d849ba-b0d3-4361-a042-26ed52b5aa79 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112005435/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-add-WR-Tavarres-King-QB-GJ-Kinne-to-practice-squad/46d849ba-b0d3-4361-a042-26ed52b5aa79 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 12, 2016 |title=Giants add WR Tavarres King, QB G.J. Kinne to practice squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 30, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=October 1, 2015}} On January 4, 2016, Kinne signed a reserve/future contract with the Giants.{{cite web |url=http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2016/01/giants_future_signings_leon_mcfadden_gj_kinne.html |title=Giants sign 6 players to reserve/future contracts |last=Raanan |first=Jordan |date=January 4, 2016 |website=[[NJ.com]] |accessdate=January 11, 2016}} On May 5, 2016, the Giants waived Kinne.{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-waive-TE-Jerome-Cunningham-safety-GJ-Kinne/1f2b0022-e29a-43a4-9453-430b4a87cca8 |title=Giants waive TE Jerome Cunningham, safety G.J. Kinne |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=May 5, 2016 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=July 18, 2016 |archive-date=October 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021014123/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-waive-TE-Jerome-Cunningham-safety-GJ-Kinne/1f2b0022-e29a-43a4-9453-430b4a87cca8 |url-status=dead }} ===Calgary Stampeders=== Kinne signed with the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on June 13, 2016.{{Cite web|url=http://www.stampeders.com/2016/06/13/stampeders-make-roster-moves-2/|title=Stampeders make roster moves|date=June 13, 2016|website=Calgary Stampeders|access-date=November 7, 2016}} Less than a week later, on June 19, 2016, Kinne was released by the team.{{Cite news|url=https://calgaryherald.com/sports/football/dickenson-explains-final-roster-moves|title=Calgary Stampeders' head coach Dave Dickenson explains final roster moves|date=June 21, 2016|newspaper=Calgary Herald|language=en-US|access-date=November 7, 2016}} ===Saskatchewan Roughriders=== Kinney signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] (CFL) on June 24, 2016.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/roughriders-add-2-more-quarterbacks-to-roster-1.3652957|title=Roughriders add 2 more quarterbacks to roster|newspaper=CBC News|access-date=November 7, 2016}} Kinne made his CFL debut in the final game of the [[2016 CFL season]], completing 4 of 11 pass attempts for 24 yards.{{Cite news|url=https://leaderpost.com/sports/football/cfl/saskatchewan-roughriders/g-j-kinne-is-ready-to-make-his-saskatchewan-roughriders-debut|title=G.J. Kinne is ready to make his Saskatchewan Roughriders debut|date=November 3, 2016|newspaper=Regina Leader-Post|language=en-US|access-date=November 7, 2016}} Kinne announced his retirement from professional football on May 9, 2017.{{Cite news|url=https://leaderpost.com/sports/football/cfl/saskatchewan-roughriders/roughriders-down-to-four-quarterbacks|title=Roughriders down to four quarterbacks|date=May 9, 2017|newspaper=Regina Leader-Post|language=en-US|access-date=May 10, 2017}} ==Coaching career== ===Early coaching career=== Kinne is from the [[Gus Malzahn]] coaching tree. In 2017, Kinne was hired as an assistant coach with [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU]] under coach [[Chad Morris]]. When Morris joined the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|University of Arkansas]] before SMU played in the [[2017 Frisco Bowl|Frisco Bowl]], new head coach [[Sonny Dykes]] chose to have Kinne serve as offensive coordinator and play caller for the bowl game.{{cite news|last=Grosbard|first=Adam|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/smu-mustangs/2017/12/14/smu-head-coach-sonny-dykes-on-why-he-trusts-graduate-assistant-g-j-kinne-to-call-plays-in-frisco-bowl/|title=SMU head coach Sonny Dykes on why he trusts graduate assistant G.J. Kinne to call plays in Frisco Bowl|newspaper=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=December 14, 2017|accessdate=December 26, 2019}}{{cite news|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2017/12/21/wednesdays-college-football-louisiana-tech-pounds-smu/108807450/|title=Wednesday's college football: Louisiana Tech pounds SMU|newspaper=[[The Detroit News]]|date=December 21, 2019|accessdate=December 26, 2019}} Kinne eventually followed Morris to Arkansas in 2018 as an offensive analyst. On February 25, 2019, Kinne was named an offensive assistant coach for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], working with special projects.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pennlive.com/philadelphiaeagles/2019/02/philadelphia-eagles-news-roundup-super-bowl-54-odds-a-coaching-staff-addition-and-more.html|title=Philadelphia Eagles news roundup: Super Bowl 54 odds, a coaching staff addition and more|last=Gallen|first=Daniel|date=February 5, 2019|website=Pennlive.com}} ===Hawaii=== On January 31, 2020, it was announced that Kinne was leaving the Eagles to become the offensive coordinator for the [[University of Hawaii at Manoa|University of Hawaii]] under head coach [[Todd Graham]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.staradvertiser.com/2020/01/31/sports/sports-breaking/hawaii-hires-gj-kinne-former-philadelphia-eagles-assistant-as-new-offensive-coordinator/|title=Hawaii hires GJ Kinne, former Philadelphia Eagles assistant, as new offensive coordinator|last=Tsai|first=Stephen|date=January 31, 2020|website=staradvertiser.com}} ===UCF=== Kinne joined the staff at [[UCF Knights football|UCF]] as their co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach in 2021, having previously played and been mentored by [[Gus Malzahn]] at Tulsa. After an injury to starting quarterback [[Dillon Gabriel]] early in the season, Kinne helped coach and mentor true freshman [[Mikey Keene]]. UCF went 9-4, winning the Gasparilla Bowl against [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] and having one of the nation's top offenses that year.{{cite web |title=UH offensive coordinator GJ Kinne to join staff at UCF |url=https://www.khon2.com/sports/report-uh-offensive-coordinator-gj-kinne-to-join-staff-at-ucf/ |website=KHON2 |date=February 21, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021}} ===Incarnate Word=== On December 21, 2021, Kinne was announced as the new head football coach at the [[University of the Incarnate Word]] (UIW).{{Cite web|url=https://uiwcardinals.com/news/2021/12/21/uiw-athletics-welcomes-g-j-kinne-as-head-football-coach.aspx|title=UIW Athletics Welcomes G.J. Kinne as Head Football Coach|date=January 30, 2022|website=uiwcardinals.com}} In his first year as a head coach, he led his team to a [[Southland Conference]] championship. UIW was the No. 7 ranked team nationally, and a seed in the FCS Playoffs. The Cardinals reached the semifinals of the 2022 FCS Playoffs and went 12-2 overall. They ranked No. 1 in all of NCAA Division I – FBS and FCS – with 51.5 points and 581.2 yards per game. The team's defense ranked first in FCS in tackles for loss, ninth in sacks, and 38th in scoring defense. Kinne was a finalist for the [[Eddie Robinson Award]] in 2022, which is presented to the nation's top coach. Quarterback [[Lindsey Scott Jr.]] was the 2022 [[Walter Payton Award]] winner under Kinne. Scott amassed 71 TDs (60 passing, 11 rushing), 4,686 yards passing, and 712 rushing.{{Cite web|url=https://uiwcardinals.com/news/2022/11/21/football-g-j-kinne-announced-as-finalist-for-eddie-robinson-award.aspx#:~:text=SAN%20ANTONIO%20%E2%80%93%20Stats%20Perform%20announced,select%20a%20winner%20on%20Dec.|title=G.J. Kinne Announced as Finalist for Eddie Robinson Award|date=November 21, 2022|website=uiwcardinals.com}} === Texas State === [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State University]] hired Kinne on December 2, 2022, to replace [[Jake Spavital]]. Kinne took over following the conclusion of Incarnate Word's season.{{Cite news |date=December 2, 2022 |title=UIW's G.J. Kinne named new Texas State head football coach |language=en |work=[[WOAI-TV]] |url=https://news4sanantonio.com/sports/content/uiws-gj-kinne-named-new-texas-state-head-football-coach |access-date=December 2, 2022}} Texas State re-signed Kinne on November 22, 2024 with a new seven-year contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/42532455/texas-state-giving-gj-kinne-new-7-year-deal-sources-say|title=Texas State giving GJ Kinne new 7-year deal, sources '''David Andrew Gregory''' is an American actor and writer. He portrayed [[Robert Ford (One Life to Live)|Robert Ford]] on the soap opera ''[[One Life to Live]]'' from 2009 until the show ended in 2012. He wrote and produced “Powder Burns”, the scripted Western podcast starring [[John Wesley Shipp]] as a blind sheriff, which premiered on Apple Podcasts in 2015 to rave reviews and earned Gregory a Voice Arts Award in 2017. On TV, he was a recurring actor on ''[[The Good Fight]]'', ''[[Insatiable (TV series)|Insatiable]]'', ''[[Constantine (TV series)|Constantine]]'', and ''[[Deception (2013 American TV series)|Deception]]''.

==Early life==
Gregory was born and raised in [[Fairbanks, Alaska]], as the middle of three sons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Actors {{!}} David A. Gregory {{!}} One Life to Live on Soap Central |url=https://www.soapcentral.com/theactors/gregory_david.php |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=soapcentral.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He danced at North Star Ballet and did plays with Fairbanks Drama Association and Fairbanks Light Opera Theater. In the summer of 2003, prior to his senior year of high school, Gregory attended [[Interlochen Arts Camp]] and took home one of the institution's top honors, The Maddy Award for Excellence in Musical Theater, for his role as the Fairy Godmother in ''[[Sweet Charity]]''.

He began his collegiate study at Baldwin-Wallace College (now [[Baldwin Wallace University]]), where appeared as Owen in Brian Friel's ''Translations'', Oberon in ''[[A Midsummer Night's Dream]]'', and as Creon in Seamus Heaney's ''[[The Burial at Thebes]]'', for which he won the theater department's award for Best Actor in a Play. In 2008, he graduated with a Bachelor of Music degree in musical theatre. The same year, he earned his Equity card while appearing in [[The Full Monty (musical)|''The Full Monty'']] for the now-defunct [[American Musical Theatre of San Jose]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-09-17 |title=American Musical Theatre's 'Full Monty' has what it takes |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2008/09/17/american-musical-theatres-full-monty-has-what-it-takes/ |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=The Mercury News |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gregory made his professional debut in 2005 at Porthouse Theater as Riff in ''[[West Side Story]]''. During college, he also appeared as Ferdinand in ''[[The Tempest]]'' for [[Great Lakes Theater]] and its sister company, [[Idaho Shakespeare Festival]].

David began a two-week stint on ABC's ''[[One Life to Live]]'' in the summer of 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-05-25 |title=One Life to Live: David A. Gregory In How Do You Know |url=https://soaps.sheknows.com/one-life-to-live/news/9181/one-life-to-live-david-a-gregory-in-how-do-you-kn/ |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=Soaps.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was offered a contract that fall and stayed with the show until its cancellation. After ''One Life to Live'' ended in 2012, Gregory guest-starred on multiple television series, including a season-long arc on the short-lived NBC series ''[[Deception (2013 American TV series)|Deception]]''. In 2014, he appeared in Hartford Stage's ''[[Vanya and Sonia and Masha and Spike]]'', earning a Connecticut Critics Circle Award nomination and appearing on the cover of ''American Theater'' magazine in the role the next year.{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}}

Gregory's audio Western, "Powder Burns," won the [[Voice Arts Award]] for Outstanding Storytelling/Best Performance for an episode dealing with Alzheimer's disease. [[John Wesley Shipp]] and [[Ed Asner]] starred opposite Gregory in the episode. [[Western Writers of America]] hailed the production as "Darn Good Entertainment. The Future of Westerns."

Gregory's play ''Hank & Jim Build a Plane'' was workshopped at the [[Last Frontier Theatre Conference]] in [[Valdez, Alaska]], and at [[Le Petit Theatre du Vieux Carre]] in New Orleans. The drama follows [[Henry Fonda]] and [[James Stewart]], best friends, movie stars, yet political opposites as they grapple with their differences on the night Henry's daughter Jane takes her famous trip to Vietnam. The play has been optioned by Tony Award-winning producers Jack W. Batman and Bruce Robert Harris at SunnySpot Productions in New York.

In June 2023, Gregory starred as Juror #8 in a sold-out run of ''[[Twelve Angry Men (story)|Twelve Angry Men]]'' at The Powerhouse Theatre in New Canaan, Connecticut.

== Personal life ==
Gregory lives and works in New York City, with his wife, Broadway performer Jennifer Noble. They have been together since college.{{Citation needed|date=August 2022}}

'''Juan José''' "'''Juanjo'''" '''Narváez Solarte''' (born 12 February 1995)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1193040616411/1330137883507/jugador/Jugador/Narvaez.htm |title=PLAYER PROFILE: NARVÁEZ |work=[[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] |access-date=1 September 2018 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411180604/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1193040616411/1330137883507/jugador/Jugador/Narvaez.htm |archive-date=11 April 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> is a Colombian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[V.League 1]] club [[Cong An Ho Chi Minh City FC|Cong An Ho Chi Minh City]]. Mainly an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]], he can also play as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cordobacf.com/noticia/juanjo-narvaez-el-primer-dia-del-nuevo-jugador-del-cordoba-club-de-futbol |title=Juanjo Narváez, el primer día del nuevo jugador del Córdoba Club de Fútbol |date=29 January 2018 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=[[Córdoba CF]] |language=es}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Deportivo Pasto===
Born in [[Pasto, Colombia|Pasto]], [[Nariño Department]], and a product of hometown team [[Deportivo Pasto]]'s youth ranks, Narváez spent his first two seasons as a senior with [[Deportivo Pasto]], scoring four goals; three in the [[Copa Colombia]] and another in the [[Categoría Primera B]]. He debuted for them in the Categoría Primera B on 9 March 2011 at 16 years and 25 days of age, making him the club's youngest ever player,<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/03/10/colombia/copa-colombia/deportivo-pasto/depor-fc/1083124/ Pasto 2-1 Depor F.C]; Soccerway, 9 March 2011</ref> and in the Categoría Primera A on 28 April 2012.<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/04/28/colombia/primera-a/itagui-ditaires/deportivo-pasto/1249887/ Itagüí 3-0 Pasto]; Soccerway, 28 April 2012.</ref>

===Real Madrid===
In November 2012, Narváez joined the [[youth academy]] of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://au.sports.yahoo.com/football/news/article/-/15538152/real-madrid-snap-up-colombian-prospect-juan-jose-narvaez/ |title=Real Madrid snap up Colombian prospect Juan Jose Narvaez |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=3 December 2012 |access-date=1 September 2018 |publisher=[[Yahoo!]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160423120813/https://au.sports.yahoo.com/football/a/15538152/real-madrid-snap-up-colombian-prospect-juan-jose-narvaez/ |archive-date=23 April 2016}}</ref> He was highly recommended by Real Madrid legend [[Zinedine Zidane]] to take into their youth system and was viewed as 'the next [[Radamel Falcao|Falcao]]' due to his goalscoring abilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.antena2.com.co/noticias/nari-o/08-12-11/el-jugador-juan-jos-narv-ez-lleg-de-inglaterra-y-puede-regresar |title=El jugador Juan José Narváez llegó de Inglaterra y puede regresar |date=8 December 2011 |first=Fernando Andrés |last=Quintero |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=Antena 2 |publisher=[[RCN Radio]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026002227/http://www.antena2.com.co/noticias/nari-o/08-12-11/el-jugador-juan-jos-narv-ez-lleg-de-inglaterra-y-puede-regresar |archive-date=26 October 2017}}</ref> Narváez made his debut for the club in the [[2013 Copa del Rey Juvenil]], where he scored two goals in three appearances as the team won the trophy, although he did not play in the final. He made his first team debut on 28 January 2012, playing the whole game in a 3–0 win over [[Zamalek SC]] in the Alkass International Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://alkassinternationalcup.com/gallery/real-madrid-zamalek/ |title=Real Madrid vs Zamalek |date=28 January 2012 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=Al Kass Football International |publisher=Netizency |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130407160428/http://alkassinternationalcup.com/gallery/real-madrid-zamalek/ |archive-date=7 April 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Narváez scored another goal against [[Rayo Vallecano]] in a 2–0 victory a week later.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://comutricolor.com/juan-jose-narvaez-7-goles-real-madrid/ |title=Juan José Narvaez completó 7 goles en la temporada con Real Madrid juvenil |date=29 September 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=ComuTricolor |language=es |publisher=[[Colombia national football team]]}}</ref> During the international break in October, Narvaez scored his first [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] for the club in a 6–1 win against Don Bosco.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/ActualidadCantera1213/Actualidad/1193040523899/1380892377269/noticia/Noticia/Asi_va_el_fin_de_semana_de_%E2%80%98La_Fabrica%E2%80%99.htm |title=Así va el fin de semana de 'La Fábrica' |date=12 October 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |first=Pedro |last=Castillo |work=[[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131012195319/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/ActualidadCantera1213/Actualidad/1193040523899/1380892377269/noticia/Noticia/Asi_va_el_fin_de_semana_de_%E2%80%98La_Fabrica%E2%80%99.htm |archive-date=12 October 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://comutricolor.com/2da-tripleta-juan-jose-narvaez-real-madrid/ |title=Segunda tripleta de Juan José Narvaez con Real Madrid |trans-title=Second hat-trick with Juan José Narváez with Real Madrid |date=18 October 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=ComuTricolor |language=es |publisher=[[Colombia national football team]]}}</ref>

{{Quote box | width=30% | align=right| quote="He's a kid that's grown up in such little time. In the campaigns with the lower squads, he's doing great. But realistically, the competition isn't as high as the [[UEFA Youth League]], where the quality around players his age is high. While he plays mostly with our reserve squads, he's improving in the process and contributing in more ways than one as we try to take advantage at certain times."|source=[[Alberto Toril]] after Narvaez's debut for [[Real Madrid Castilla]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.elpais.com.co/deportes/el-pastuso-juanjo-narvaez-debuto-con-real-madrid-castilla.html |title=El pastuso 'Juanjo' Narváez debutó con Real Madrid Castilla |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |author=EFE |author-link=EFE |newspaper=[[El País (Colombia)|El País]] |language=es}}</ref>}}

Narváez made his [[UEFA Youth League]] debut against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], as he managed to score the tying goal in a 1–1 draw. As of September 2013, he had scored six goals in three appearances for the U-17 squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://comutricolor.com/juan-jose-narvaez-goleador-real-madrid-juvenil/ |title=Juan José Narvaez completó 6 goles en 3 partidos con Real Madrid juvenil |date=21 September 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=ComuTricolor |language=es |publisher=[[Colombia national football team]]}}</ref> In a [[UEFA Youth League]] match against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], Narváez scored four goals, one with a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]], and also assisted the fourth goal in a 6–2 victory. This made him joint top scorer at the time with five goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2012910--real-madrid-vs-juventus/ |title=Narváez stars as Madrid overwhelm Juve |date=25 October 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=[[UEFA.com]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026071345/http://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/season=2014/matches/round=2000501/match=2012910/index.html |archive-date=26 October 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his third match representing the C team, Narváez scored his first goal against [[CF Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]], in the 82nd minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/ActualidadCantera1314/1330170398822/noticia/Cronica/3-2:_El_Real_Madrid_C_remonta_y_derrota_al_Fuenlabrada.htm |title=3-2: El Real Madrid C remonta y derrota al Fuenlabrada |trans-title=Real Madrid C complete a comeback over Fuenlabrada |first=Javi |last=Vázquez |date=30 October 2013 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=[[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131101020458/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/ActualidadCantera1314/1330170398822/noticia/Cronica/3-2:_El_Real_Madrid_C_remonta_y_derrota_al_Fuenlabrada.htm |archive-date=1 November 2013 |language=es |url-status=live }}</ref> Narváez was once again promoted, this time to [[Real Madrid Castilla]], where he came off the bench in the 88th minute.<ref name="elpais.com.co"/> Narvaez would then score his first goal against [[SD Leioa|Leioa]] in his 5th appearance.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://comutricolor.com/colombiano-juan-jose-narvaez-anoto-gol-real-madrid/ |title=El colombiano Juan José Narváez anotó gol con el Real Madrid |trans-title=Colombian Juan José Narváez scored a goal with Real Madrid |date=11 October 2014 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=ComuTricolor |language=es |publisher=[[Colombia national football team]]}}</ref>

===Betis===
At the start of the year 2016, Narváez signed for [[Real Betis]] on a three-year deal, being initially assigned to [[Real Betis B|the B-team]].<ref name="elpais.com.co">{{cite news |url=https://www.elpais.com.co/deportes/juan-jose-narvaez-nuevo-delantero-del-real-betis-b.html |title=Juan José Narváez, nuevo delantero del Real Betis B |trans-title=Juan José Narváez, new forward of Betis B |date=26 January 2016 |access-date=1 September 2018 |newspaper=[[El País (Colombia)|El País]] |language=es}}</ref> On 29 January 2018, Narváez he was loaned to [[Segunda División]] side [[Córdoba CF]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cordobacf.com/noticia/juanjo-narvaez-el-primer-dia-del-nuevo-jugador-del-cordoba-club-de-futbol |title=Juanjo Narváez, el primer día del nuevo jugador del Córdoba Club de Fútbol |trans-title=Juanjo Narváez, the first day of Córdoba Club de Fútbol's new player |publisher=Córdoba CF |language=es |date=29 January 2018 |access-date=1 September 2018}}</ref> where he helped to avoid relegation in the last game of the season by winning 3–0 to [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/liga-segunda-division/20180602/444024650299/cordoba-sporting-cronica-salvacion-permanencia-sandoval.html |title=El Córdoba se salva goleando al Sporting |trans-title=El Córdoba is saved by thrashing Sporting |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |date=2 June 2018 |access-date=1 September 2018}}</ref>

On 31 August 2018, Narváez joined [[UD Almería|Almería]] on a one-season loan.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.udalmeriasad.com/noticia/el-almeria-cierra-su-plantilla-con-la-incorporacion-del-colombiano-narvaez |title=El Almería cierra su plantilla con la incorporación del colombiano Narváez |date=31 August 2018 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=UD Almería |language=es}}</ref> Upon returning, he was initially assigned to Betis' first team in [[La Liga]], but moved to [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] still in the second division on loan for one year on 31 August 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/noticia/el-centrocampista-juanjo-narvaez-llega-cedido-del-real-betis|title=El centrocampista Juanjo Narváez llega cedido del Real Betis|trans-title=Central midfielder Juanjo Narváez arrives on loan from Real Betis|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=31 August 2019|accessdate=31 August 2019}}</ref>

===Zaragoza===
On 4 September 2020, Narváez agreed to a three-year contract with second division side [[Real Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realzaragoza.com/noticias/juanjo-narv-ez-nuevo-fichaje-del-real-zaragoza|title=Juanjo Narváez, nuevo fichaje del Real Zaragoza|trans-title=Juanjo Narváez, new signing of Real Zaragoza|publisher=Real Zaragoza|language=es|date=4 September 2020|accessdate=4 September 2020}}</ref> An undisputed starter, he scored nine goals in [[2020–21 Segunda División|his first season]].

===Valladolid===
On 1 September 2022, Narváez signed a two-year contract with [[Real Valladolid]] in the top tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticia/narvaez-completa-el-puzzle|title=Narváez completa el puzzle|trans-title=Narváez completes the puzzle|publisher=Real Valladolid|language=es|date=1 September 2022|accessdate=2 September 2022}}</ref> The following 30 January, after being rarely used, he returned to the second division after being loaned to [[CD Leganés]] until the end of [[2022–23 Segunda División|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdleganes.com/noticias/el-cd-leganes-refuerza-su-ataque-con-juanjo-narvaez|title=El C.D. Leganés refuerza su ataque con Juanjo Narváez|trans-title=C.D. Leganés bolster their attack with Juanjo Narváez|publisher=CD Leganés|language=es|date=30 January 2023|accessdate=31 January 2023}}</ref>

On 23 August 2023, Narváez terminated his contract with the ''Pucelanos''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticias/narvaez-no-sigue-en-el-pucela|title=Narváez no sigue en el Pucela|trans-title=Narváez does not continue at ''Pucela''|publisher=Real Valladolid|language=es|date=23 August 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023}}</ref>

===Cartagena===
On 23 August 2023, just hours after leaving Valladolid, Narváez signed a two-year contract with [[FC Cartagena]] in the second division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fccartagena.es/noticias/juanjo-narvaez-potencia-y-verticalidad-para-el-frente-de-ataque-del-efese|title=Juanjo Narváez, potencia y verticalidad para el frente de ataque del Efesé|trans-title=Juanjo Narváez, power and verticality for the front lines of the ''Efesé''|publisher=FC Cartagena|language=es|date=23 August 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023}}</ref> On 9 August of the following year, he terminated his link with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fccartagena.es/noticias/acuerdo-con-juanjo-narvaez-para-la-rescision-de-su-contrato|title=Acuerdo con Juanjo Narváez para la rescisión de su contrato|trans-title=Agreement with Juanjo Narváez for the rescision of his contract|publisher=FC Cartagena|language=es|date=9 August 2024|accessdate=12 August 2024}}</ref>

===Saudi Arabia===
On 31 August 2024, Narváez joined [[Saudi First Division League]] club [[Al-Jabalain FC|Al-Jabalain]].<ref>{{cite web |title=رسمياً الأسباني جوانجو نارفيز جبلاوياً |url=https://x.com/aljabalainFC/status/1829829885365223927}}</ref>

On 5 September 2025, Narváez joined [[Al-Raed FC|Al-Raed]].<ref>{{cite web |title=عائلة #الرائد تضم نجمنا الجديد الكولمبي خوان نارفيز |url=https://x.com/alraedclub/status/1964002534340612351}}</ref>

===Cong An Ho Chi Minh City===
On 13 August 2026, Narváez moved to Vietnam, signing for [[V.League 1]] side [[Cong An Ho Chi Minh City FC|Cong An Ho Chi Minh City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thethaovanhoa.vn/clb-cong-an-tphcm-chieu-mo-cau-thu-truong-thanh-tu-real-madrid-20260813094338689.htm|title=CLB Công an TP.HCM chiêu mộ cầu thủ trưởng thành từ Real Madrid|publisher=Thể Thao & Văn Hóa|date=13 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Narváez was repeatedly called up to participate in Colombia's U20 squad, but Real Madrid refused to release him; he was not allowed to take part in the [[2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://miseleccion.co/audio_programas/archivo_de_audio/real-madrid-no-quiere-prestar-a-juan-jose-narvaez-ya-no-hay-caso-piscis-resptrepo/20150104/oir/2700637.aspx |title=Real Madrid no quiere prestar a Juan José Narváez, ya no hay caso: Piscis Resptrepo |date=1 April 2015 |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=Mi Selección |language=es |publisher=Prisa}}</ref>

'''Léo Legrand''' is a French actor. He is best known for playing the role of Jacquou in ''[[Jacquou Le Croquant]]'', Thomas in ''[[Trouble at Timpetill]]'' and playing the role of Thomas Verniaz in ''[[A Distant Neighborhood (film)|A Distant Neighborhood]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.institut-francais.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/Educational_resources_Timpelbach.pdf|title=LES ENFANTS DE TIMPELBACH|accessdate=|first=|last=|date=30 May 2004|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924035312/http://www.institut-francais.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/Educational_resources_Timpelbach.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> The latter film earned him a [[Young Artist Award]] nomination in the category of [[32nd Young Artist Awards#Best Performance in an International Feature Film|Best Young Performer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.youngartistawards.org/noms32.html |title=32nd Annual Young Artist Awards |accessdate=15 January 2018|publisher= Young Artist Association|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130808150433/http://www.youngartistawards.org/noms32.html|archivedate=8 August 2013 }}</ref>

'''The Vixen''' is the stage name of '''Anthony Prince Taylor''',<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dazeddigital.com/projects/article/39796/1/the-vixen-drag-queen-biography-dazed-100-profile-2018|title=Vote for The Vixen on the #Dazed100|last=Dazed|date=2018-04-24|work=Dazed|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/song/tea-party/1445626056 |title=Tea Party |website=music.apple.com |publisher=Apple Inc. |access-date=October 16, 2023}}</ref> an American [[Drag queen|drag performer]] best known for competing on the [[RuPaul's Drag Race (season 10)|tenth season]] of ''[[RuPaul's Drag Race]]'' and placing seventh. Her appearance on the show was notable for raising a conversation around racial dynamics, both among her fellow drag queens and in the show's fandom.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.them.us/story/the-vixen-racism-drag-race|title=How The Vixen Exposed the Racism of RuPaul's Drag Race|work=them.|access-date=2018-10-09|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Billboard">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/pride/8296851/the-vixen-racial-narratives-drag-race-reactions|title='RuPaul's Drag Race' Alum React to The Vixen Breaking Down Racial Narratives Created by Fans|magazine=Billboard|access-date=2018-10-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.intomore.com/culture/the-vixen-speaks-on-season-10-reunion-and-how-rupaul-and-drag-race-fail-black-queens|title=INTO: A Digital Magazine for The Modern Queer World|newspaper=Into|date=21 June 2018 |language=en|access-date=2018-10-09|last1=Rodriguez |first1=Mathew }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://nylon.com/articles/rupaul-drag-race-the-vixen-reunion|title='RuPaul's Drag Race' Reunion Put A Spotlight On The Show's Race Problem|date=2018-06-22|work=NYLON|access-date=2018-10-09|language=en}}</ref> She is the founder of ''Black Girl Magic'', a drag show consisting of only African-American queens. In August 2020, she released ''Commercial Break'', her debut album.

== Early life ==
Taylor was born to Sheri Jones.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=TheVixensworld |number=430039193189117953 |title=its My Mommy's Bday!! LOVE U XOXO!!! Sheri Jones <3<3<3}}</ref> He started doing drag at a local bar called the Jeffery Pub in April 2013. His [[drag mother]] is Savannah Westbrooke.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/vixen-rupaul-drag-race-jeffery-pub-block-beat-triibe/Content?oid=48135666|title=The Vixen revisits the starting line of her personal drag race|last=Johnson|first=The TRiiBE, Tiffany Walden, Morgan Elise|work=Chicago Reader|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref> The drag name "The Vixen" comes from his love of 1920s [[Vintage clothing|vintage wear]], and the word "vixen" comes in those searches.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.chicagomag.com/Chicago-Magazine/September-2017/Drag-Queen-Fashion/|title=Queens for a Day: Fall Fashion Goes Drag|work=Chicago magazine|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref>

==Career ==
The Vixen is known for blending political activism and queer advocacy into her drag performances.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bustle.com/p/after-rupauls-drag-race-the-vixen-says-her-activism-is-only-just-beginning-9063777|title=The Vixen Has Big Plans After 'RuPaul's Drag Race'|last=Blanton|first=Kayla|work=Bustle|access-date=2018-10-09|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Tucker">{{Cite news|url=https://chicagoreader.com/arts-culture/chicagos-black-drag-queens-are-upholding-a-radical-gender-bending-tradition/|title=Chicago's black drag queens are upholding a radical gender-bending tradition|last=Tucker|first=KT Hawbaker, Sunshine|work=Chicago Reader|access-date=2025-05-30}}</ref> She has been an outspoken critic about [[anti-black sentiment]] in America, including in white queer communities, stating, "you [often] have to choose between calling out [[racism]] or [[homophobia]]".<ref name="Tucker"/>

In November 2016, Taylor founded ''Black Girl Magic'', a drag show consisting of only African-American queens. ''Drag Race'' alumni [[DiDa Ritz]] and [[Shea Couleé]] were part of the first show.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://chicago.gopride.com/news/article.cfm/articleid/86059984|title=That 'Black Girl Magic' has us in its spell|last=Morgano|first=Anthony|work=ChicagoPride.com|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-06-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622084022/http://chicago.gopride.com/news/article.cfm/articleid/86059984|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://chicago.gopride.com/news/article.cfm/articleid/96876244/black-girl-magic-shows-unite-queens-of-color-we-are-stronger-together|title=Black Girl Magic shows unite Queens of Color: 'We are stronger together'|last=Forman|first=Ross|work=ChicagoPride.com|access-date=2018-08-03|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-08-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803104110/http://chicago.gopride.com/news/article.cfm/articleid/96876244/black-girl-magic-shows-unite-queens-of-color-we-are-stronger-together|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her fellow season ten contestants [[Asia O'Hara]], [[Monét X Change]] and [[Monique Heart]] were added to the line-up of the ''Black Girl Magic'' cast in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/black-girl-magic-with-asia-ohara-monet-x-change-monique-heart-the-vixen-shea-coulee-dida-ritz-bambi-banks-eva-styles-lucy-stoole-and/Event?oid=48032826|title=Black Girl Magic with Asia O'Hara, Monét X Change, Monique Heart, the Vixen, Shea Coulee, Dida Ritz, Bambi Banks, Eva Styles, Lucy Stoole, and Sasha Love|website=Chicago Reader|date=23 September 2009|language=en|access-date=2018-10-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.showclix.com/event/black-girl-magic-chicago|title=Black Girl Magic|website=ShowClix|date=26 June 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-02}}</ref>

The Vixen was announced as one of fourteen contestants for season ten of ''RuPaul's Drag Race'' on February 22, 2018.<ref name=drs10>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2018/02/23/rupauls-drag-race-season-10-meet-14-fierce-drag-queens/366718002/|title='RuPaul's Drag Race' Season 10: Meet the 14 fierce drag queens|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref> She won the episode two main challenge.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bustle.com/p/will-the-vixen-win-rupauls-drag-race-season-10-shes-proven-herself-to-be-a-frontrunner-8588817|title=Why The Vixen Could Absolutely Win 'RuPaul's Drag Race'|last=Koch|first=Drew|work=Bustle|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref> In the third episode, she engaged in a verbal back-and-forth with fellow contestant [[Aquaria (drag queen)|Aquaria]], which left Aquaria crying and The Vixen noting that the exchange "created the narrative [of] an angry black woman who has scared off the little white girl".<ref name="Billboard"/> Although Aquaria eventually conceded the point and later came to her defense, The Vixen received online [[death threats]] from ''Drag Race'' fans afterwards.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/pride/8299834/aquaria-calls-out-racist-fans-drag-race|title='RuPaul's Drag Race' Queen Aquaria Calls Out Racist Fans for Threatening The Vixen: 'Jump Off the Aquaria Train'|magazine=Billboard|access-date=2018-06-22}}</ref> She faced more backlash after quarreling with competitor [[Eureka O'Hara]] in multiple episodes, most notably in episode 4 of ''[[Untucked]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vh1.com/news/dzbht0/the-vixen-hates-eurekas-snatch-game-performance|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728011907/https://www.vh1.com/news/dzbht0/the-vixen-hates-eurekas-snatch-game-performance|url-status=live|archive-date=July 28, 2023|title=Everyone Was In Love With Eureka's Snatch Game Performance as Honey Boo Boo...Except For The Vixen|work=VH1 News|access-date=2018-06-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fandom.wikia.com/articles/monique-heart-interview-drag-race-power-rankings|title='Drag Race' Exclusive: Monique Heart Takes a Side in Vixen/Eureka Feud|date=2018-05-04|work=[[FANDOM]]|publisher=Wikia, Inc.|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/pride/8455656/drag-race-the-vixen-interview|title='Drag Race:' The Vixen Sends Her Haters a Message: 'You're Uncomfortable Because I Am Creating Change'|magazine=Billboard|access-date=2018-06-22}}</ref> She was eliminated in seventh place after losing a lip sync to "[[Groove Is in the Heart]]" against Asia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.popbuzz.com/tv-film/rupauls-drag-race/season-10-episode-8-review/|title=Drag Race Season 10 Episode 8 Review: Cher The Rusical!|work=PopBuzz|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref> During the final reunion episode, she walked offstage after feeling cornered by moderator and host [[RuPaul]] who kept pressing her to revisit past confrontations with Aquaria and Eureka.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tvline.com/recaps/rupauls-drag-race-recap-season-10-reunion-the-vixen-fight-958048/|title=RuPaul's Drag Race Season 10 Reunion: Who Made Nice? And Who Walked Off?|last=Swift|first=Andy|date=2018-06-22|work=TVLine|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en-US}}</ref> [[RuPaul's Drag Race (season 6)|Season six]] alum [[Courtney Act]] later criticized RuPaul for a lack of compassion during the exchange.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://intomore.com/culture/courtney-act-on-rupaul-racism-and-living-her-dream-post-celebrity-big-brother|title=INTO: A Digital Magazine for The Modern Queer World|website=intomore.com|date=12 July 2018 |language=en|access-date=2018-08-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2018/08/01/courtney-act-calls-drag-race-social-experiment-unconscious-bias-addresses-series-10-race-row-7782754/|title=Courtney Act calls Drag Race a 'social experiment on unconscious bias'|date=2018-08-01|work=Metro|access-date=2018-08-03|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Outside of ''Drag Race'', The Vixen had a booth covered with the ''Black Girl Magic'' logo for the first annual [[Wakanda]]con in August 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.vh1.com/news/364815/rupauls-drag-race-the-vixen-slays-wakandacon-chicago/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808000336/http://www.vh1.com/news/364815/rupauls-drag-race-the-vixen-slays-wakandacon-chicago/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 8, 2018|title=The Vixen Showed Up and Showed Out at Chicago's First Ever Wakandacon Convention|work=VH1 News|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref>

She became a sponsor for [[Grindr]]'s "''Kindr''{{-"}} [[public service announcement]] in September 2018, in an effort to stop racial discrimination in the app.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.gq.com/story/can-grindr-make-itself-less-racist|title=Can Grindr Make Itself Less Racist?|last=Wheeler|first=André|date=2018-09-11|work=GQ|access-date=2018-09-17|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
The Vixen is [[Gay men|gay]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pride.com/thevixen/2018/6/18/vixen-drag-queen-safer-world-black-man|title=The Vixen: 'A Drag Queen Is Safer in This World Than a Black Man'|date=2018-06-18|access-date=2018-08-03|language=en}}</ref> Her former drag daughter is Delikate Doll.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/thevixensworld/status/999825880712208384|title=The Vixen on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=2018-06-22|language=en}}</ref> In 2023, she announced that she had moved from Chicago to [[New Orleans]], Louisiana.<ref>{{Cite instagram |user=thevixensworld |postid=CwGOWy9pCX |title=I keep forgetting to say officially that I've moved from Chicago to New Orleans |date=August 18, 2023}}</ref>

'''Nicholas Foster Rattigan''' (born August 6, 1992) is an American multi-instrumentalist, singer, and songwriter from [[Reno, Nevada]]. He currently releases music under the moniker '''Current Joys'''. He also is the drummer and lead singer of the [[Independent music|indie]] [[Surf music|surf rock]] band [[Surf Curse]]. As an artist, Rattigan began releasing music as '''The Nicholas Project''' from 2011 to 2012, thereafter releasing music as '''TELE/VISIONS''', releasing his debut album, ''Wild Heart'', in January 2013, as well as all of his music on [[Bandcamp]].

After 2015, Rattigan began performing as Current Joys, with his second studio album ''Me Oh My Mirror'', released in February 2015, reflecting the significant change in his style of music.

He released his third album, ''A Different Age'', in March 2018. His fourth album, ''Voyager'', was released in May 2021. He released his fifth album, ''LOVE + POP'', in August 2023. The sequel, ''LOVE + POP Pt 2'', was released in May 2024. He released his seventh album, ''East My Love'' in October 2024. His singles "Kids" and "Televisions" were featured in the 2025 horror film ''[[Obsession (2025 film)|Obsession]]''.

== Career ==
=== 2011–2015 ===
Rattigan started individually writing and releasing music as The Nicholas Project, after an anonymous [[Myspace]] message inspired him to compose music. He self-released a slew of independently produced recordings on [[Bandcamp]] from November 2011 to October 2012 under the moniker.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thenicholasproject.bandcamp.com/album/the-basement-tapes|title=The Basement Tapes by The Nicholas Project|date=November 14, 2011|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thenicholasproject.bandcamp.com/track/la-dream|title=LA Dream by The Nicholas Project|date=October 11, 2012|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

As TELE/VISIONS, Rattigan self-released his debut album, ''Wild Heart'', on January 2, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/wild-heart|title=Wild Heart by TELE/VISIONS|date=January 2, 2013|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> Citing the name change as being influenced by ''[[Videodrome]]'', Rattigan said to ''FORGE Magazine'' that "I was writing this song and my roommate had given me a drum machine, so I was like "This is perfect! I can start playing live shows!" and they were like "yeah but no one is going to book you with your name as the Nicholas Project" and they were right."<ref name="James-Wilson 2018" />

In 2013, Rattigan and classmate Jacob Rubeck, who self-releases music under the moniker Gap Girls (Previously Casino Hearts),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://casinohearts.bandcamp.com/|title=Casino Hearts on Bandcamp|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> formed the band [[Surf Curse]]. This [[Surf punk (music genre)|surf punk]] band would be their second major project after a small project named Buffalo 66.<ref>{{Cite news|last=James-Wilson|first=Matthew|date=July 31, 2017|title=FORGE. Issue 16: Perspective|work=FORGE.|publisher=[[issuu]]|url=https://issuu.com/forgeartmag/docs/issuu16/92|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> Through Big Joy Records, an independent label in Los Angeles, California, they released their debut album, ''Buds'', in June 2013<ref>{{Cite web|title=Buds, by Surf Curse|url=https://surfcurse.bandcamp.com/album/buds|access-date=2020-09-30|website=Surf Curse}}</ref> and the [[extended play]] (EP) ''Sad Boys EP'' in October.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sad Boys EP, by Surf Curse|url=https://surfcurse.bandcamp.com/album/sad-boys-ep|access-date=2020-09-30|website=Surf Curse}}</ref>

Three EPs were released in 2013: ''Young Luv'' in January,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/young-luv-ep|title=Young Luv EP by TELE/VISIONS|date=January 19, 2013|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> ''No One Will Dance'' in February<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/no-one-will-dance|title=No One Will Dance by TELE/VISIONS|date=February 13, 2013|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> and ''Neon Gold'' in June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/neon-gold|title=Neon Gold by TELE/VISIONS|date=June 23, 2013|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> Also, from May to July 2013, Rattigan wrote for Noisey, a brand under ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://noisey.vice.com/en_us/contributor/nick-rattigan|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305142908/https://noisey.vice.com/en_us/contributor/nick-rattigan|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 5, 2018|title=Nick Rattigan – Noisey|website=Noisey|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

An extended play, ''2013'', was released in January 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/2013|title=2013 by TELE/VISIONS|date=January 21, 2014|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> ''2008–2010'', a compilation album, was released as the final work under The Nicholas Project in May.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thenicholasproject.bandcamp.com/album/2008-2010|title=2008–2010 by The Nicholas Project|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> A compilation of b-sides and unreleased tracks, ''B-Sides, Rarities and Demos'', was released a month later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://televisionsss.bandcamp.com/album/b-sides-rarities-and-demos|title=B-Sides, Rarities and Demos by TELE/VISIONS|date=June 5, 2014|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

Rattigan wrote for ''[[Impose (magazine)|Impose]]'' as an intern from September to October 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.imposemagazine.com/profile/nick-rattigan|title=Nick Rattigan|work=[[Impose (magazine)|Impose]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

Found on his YouTube channel, Rattigan has performed under additional names, [[Franco Years]] and Devil Worship. Both of these projects can be found on Bandcamp.

=== 2015–present ===
In February 2015, Rattigan announced that the follow-up to ''Wild Heart'' was almost complete.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/currentjoys/photos/a.791257194228467.1073741829.628160127204842/902966913057494/|title=Current Joys – New album is almost done. Should be out...|date=February 4, 2015|website=Facebook|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}} The album, ''Me Oh My Mirror'', was then self-released on February 16.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://currentjoys.bandcamp.com/album/me-oh-my-mirror|title=Me Oh My Mirror by Current Joys|date=February 16, 2015|website=[[Bandcamp]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

In January 2016, the limited-edition [[zine]] ''Alabama (2000 Light Years)'' was announced for release in February.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/currentjoys/photos/a.654552841232237.1073741828.628160127204842/1076592839028233/|title=Current Joys – Zine release show Feb 13th at The Smell...|date=January 24, 2016|website=Facebook|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}}

On March 6, 2016, the song "New Flesh" from ''Wild Heart'' was used in a short video titled "Flesh" on [[Vine (service)|Vine]] by Internet celebrity Emma Greer, under her online alias GIBBERTON. The video was her last before her death from cancer twenty-one days later and caused a rise in interest towards the song.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/alyssa6hogan/status/714978164410228736|title=@emmagreerie I want to know the songg|date=March 29, 2016|website=Twitter|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}} Two days later, Rattigan released a song, "Kids", and announced the name change to Current Joys instead of TELE/VISIONS, stating that "I no longer feel like it represents the music I want to make and there are too many conflicts with the band Television which present problems for future prospects."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/currentjoys/posts/918462294841289|title=Current Joys – Dear close friends and supporters, I have...|date=March 8, 2015|website=Facebook|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}} To fit with the change, Rattigan re-released all of his music under the moniker in October.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/currentjoys/photos/a.654552841232237.1073741828.628160127204842/1273336362687212/?type=3|title=Current Joys – My entire discography (previously released...|date=October 26, 2016|website=Facebook|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}}

Rattigan, debuting as a [[music video director]], produced and directed the music video for "123" by the folk punk band [[Girlpool]] in March 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.stereogum.com/1928100/girlpool-123-video/video/|title=Girlpool – "123" Video|last=Rettig|first=James|date=March 6, 2017|work=[[Stereogum]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.spin.com/2017/03/girlpool-new-album-powerplant-123/|title=New Music: Girlpool Announce New Album Powerplant, Share "123"|last=Cook-Wilson|first=Winston|date=March 6, 2017|work=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|access-date=March 5, 2018}}</ref> In July, Rattigan released a second limited-edition zine entitled ''Days'', which came with an unreleased five-song EP.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/currentjoys/photos/a.654552841232237.1073741828.628160127204842/1544960932191419/|title=Current Joys – Hey everyone! Sorry I've been quiet on...|date=July 11, 2017|website=Facebook|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2019}} He also collaborated with labelmate BOYO for a 4-track EP, ''Split'', released by Danger Collective and Terrible Records on September 6.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://store.dangercollective.com/products/599294-current-joys-boyo-split|title=Current Joys / BOYO – Split|website=Danger Collective|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref>

On January 8, "Become The Warm Jets" and "Fear" were released as the lead singles for ''A Different Age'', his debut album on Danger Collective.<ref name="Israelsohn 2018" /> The music video for "In a Year of 13 Moons", named after a 1978 film by [[Rainer Werner Fassbinder]], was released on January 30 as the third single.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ozs2pnP0gq8|title=Current Joys – In a Year of 13 Moons|date=January 30, 2018|publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> In February, the fourth single from the album, "My Nights Are More Beautiful Than Your Days", titled after [[My Nights Are More Beautiful Than Your Days|the film of the same name]], premiered on [[L.A. Record]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://larecord.com/news/2018/02/14/video-premiere-current-joys-my-nights-are-more-beautiful-than-your-days|title=VIDEO PREMIERE: CURRENT JOYS "MY NIGHTS ARE MORE BEAUTIFUL THAN YOUR DAYS"|date=February 14, 2018|work=[[L.A. Record]]|access-date=March 4, 2018|archive-date=April 9, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409225900/https://larecord.com/news/2018/02/14/video-premiere-current-joys-my-nights-are-more-beautiful-than-your-days|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album was released on March 2. Within the same month, [[NPR]] included "Fear" in "The Austin 100", a playlist of songs from artists performing at SXSW.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2018/03/01/588748343/the-austin-100-current-joys|title=The Austin 100: Current Joys|last=Thompson|first=Steven|date=March 1, 2018|publisher=[[NPR]]|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> His 2023 album, ''LOVE + POP,'' featured an unexpected feature from popular American rapper and singer [[Lil Yachty]] on the track "Gatsby". His 2024 album, ''LOVE + POP Pt 2,'' contained collaborations from Gonerville, Brutus VIII, [[FearDorian]], and [[1nonly]]. In October of the same year, he released ''East My Love''.<ref>{{cite web
