'''Camilla Huseby''' (born 12 April 1999) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a defender for Norwegian First Division club [[Kolbotn Fotball|Kolbotn IL]].

==Career==
Born in Lørenskog at [[Akershus University Hospital]],<ref name=wf/> she grew up in [[Ås, Norway|Ås]] and started her career in [[Ås IL]].<ref name=aas/> She made her international debut for Norway U15 in 2014, as she also joined the bigger neighboring club, [[Kolbotn Fotball|Kolbotn IL]]. Her [[Toppserien]] debut came in August 2015, in a 10–0 thrashing of Medkila, followed by her first Toppserien goal in November 2016 against Trondheims-Ørn.<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3715214}}</ref>

In the [[2017 Norwegian First Division (women)|2017 First Division]], Huseby had changed clubs to [[Lyn Fotball Damer|Lyn]] and was named Player of the Year. The team won promotion to the Toppserien in the same year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/camilla-huseby/sport/toppserien/camilla-huseby-ble-arets-spiller-i-1-divisjon/s/5-68-341660|title=Camilla Huseby ble årets spiller i 1. divisjon|date=18 November 2017|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> She contested the [[2018 UEFA Women's Under-19 Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/sport/as/linn-og-camilla-huseby/fotballtvillingene-linn-19-og-camilla-19-fra-as-spiller-i-em/s/5-68-444895|title=Fotballtvillingene Linn (19) og Camilla (19) fra Ås spiller i EM|date=18 July 2018|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> After three seasons in Lyn, Huseby needed "a new challenge".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.svd.se/a/dOBz6z/norsk-mittback-till-djurgarden|title=Norsk mittback till Djurgården|date=28 January 2020|work=Svenska Dagbladet|agency=TT|language=sv|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> In 2020 she was persuaded to move to the [[Damallsvenskan]] with [[Djurgårdens IF Fotboll (women)|Djurgårdens IF]].<ref name=aas>{{cite news|url=https://www.aasavis.no/as-jenta-camilla-21-gikk-til-svensk-fotball-lonna-er-hoyere-med-det-var-ikke-penger-som-lokket-meg/s/5-2-441813|title=Ås-jenta Camilla (21) gikk til svensk fotball. – Lønna er høyere med det var ikke penger som lokket meg|date=21 May 2020|work=Ås Avis|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> The [[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]] and [[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway|Norway]] meant a curtailing of the free travel between the countries, and as such, Huseby chose to move back to Norway after the 2020 campaign.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fotbollskanalen.se/bloggar/sillybloggen/officiellt-huseby-lamnar-djurgarden|title=Officiellt: Huseby lämnar Djurgården|date=1 December 2020|work=Fotbollskanalen|language=sv|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref>

She joined [[Vålerenga Fotball Damer|Vålerenga]], the [[Battle of Oslo (football)|rival]] of her former club Lyn,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://vartoslo.no/bydel-gamle-oslo-camilla-huseby-eli-landsem/jeg-hadde-fine-ar-i-lyn-men-na-er-jeg-valerenga-jente-sier-camilla-huseby-21/272926|title=- Jeg hadde fine år i Lyn, men nå er jeg Vålerenga-jente, sier Camilla Huseby (21)|date=1 December 2020|work=Vårt Oslo|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> then went on to Vålerenga's other [[Lillestrøm SK-Vålerenga Fotball rivalry|rival]], [[LSK Kvinner FK]] ahead of the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/etter-overgangen-fra-vif-straler-camilla-24-pa-fotballbanen-godt-at-folk-har-trua-pa-meg/s/5-43-2001264|title=Etter overgangen fra VIF stråler Camilla (24) på fotballbanen: – Godt at folk har trua på meg|date=20 April 2023|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref> In January 2025, Huseby rejoined her childhood club Kolbotn.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oavis.no/arild-sundgot-camilla-huseby-kolbotn-fotball-kvinner/toppserie-profil-gjor-comeback-i-kolbotn/1005934|title=Toppserie-profil gjør comeback i Kolbotn|date=6 January 2025|work=Oppegård Avis|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is a twin sister of [[Linn Huseby]]. They played for the same teams until 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/for-forste-gang-er-linn-20-uten-tvillingsosteren-ved-sin-side-det-er-rart/s/5-68-791887|title=For første gang er Linn (20) uten tvillingsøsteren ved sin side: – Det er rart|date=26 February 2020|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/ingen-har-betydd-mer-for-camilla-enn-tvillingsosteren-na-er-de-konkurrenter-vanskelig-a-beskrive/s/5-43-1947192|title=Ingen har betydd mer for Camilla enn tvillingsøsteren – nå er de konkurrenter: – Vanskelig å beskrive|date=16 January 2023|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Caterina Ambrosi''' (born 1999) is an Italian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Serie A Women|Serie A]] club [[Parma Calcio 2022|Parma]]. She is the captain of Parma's women's first team.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Caterina Ambrosi called up to the national team for the friendlies against Japan and Brazil
 |url=https://www.parmacalcio1913.com/en/main-news/caterina-ambrosi-convocata-in-nazionale-per-le-amichevoli-con-giappone-e-brasile/
 |website=Parma Calcio 1913
 |date=15 October 2025
 |access-date=8 September 2026
}}</ref>

==Club career==

Ambrosi became captain of Parma's women's team and was part of the side that won promotion to [[Serie A (women's football)|Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Parma Women, Valenti: «Vorrei una squadra coraggiosa»
 |url=https://www.gazzettadiparma.it/home/2025/07/17/news/parma-women-valenti-vorrei-una-squadra-coraggiosa-879873/
 |website=Gazzetta di Parma
 |date=17 July 2025
 |access-date=8 September 2026
}}</ref>

According to ''Gazzetta di Parma'', from the 2023–24 season through October 2025, Ambrosi made 69 appearances and scored 17 goals for Parma, while helping the club achieve promotion to Serie A and subsequently establishing herself as a regular in the top division.<ref>{{cite news
 |title=Caterina Ambrosi convocata in Nazionale
 |url=https://www.dagmar-reichardt.net/files/download/Gazzetta_di_Parma_16_Ottobre_2025__p._27.pdf
 |work=Gazzetta di Parma
 |date=16 October 2025
 |access-date=8 September 2026
}}</ref>

In 2026, Ambrosi was named in the [[Serie A Women]] Team of the Season for the 2025–26 season at the Athora Game On – All Stars Night.<ref name="FIGC">{{cite web
 |title=Athora Game On, All Stars Night: Domenico Aurelio and Caterina Ambrosi recognised
 |url=https://www.parmacalcio1913.com/en/main-news/athora-game-on-all-stars-night-domenico-aurelio-and-caterina-ambrosi-recognised
 |website=Parma Calcio 1913
 |date=19 May 2026
 |access-date=8 September 2026
}}</ref>

==International career==

In October 2025, Ambrosi received her first call-up to the [[Italy women's national football team|Italy women's national team]] for friendly matches against [[Japan women's national football team|Japan]] and [[Brazil women's national football team|Brazil]]. She was one of 30 players selected by head coach [[Andrea Soncin]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=30 Azzurre called up for friendlies against Japan and Brazil: first call-up for Ambrosi and Corelli
 |url=https://files.figc.it/view/acePublic/alias/contentid/1mnxmjrk8k7nzh1isaw/1/Media%20Kit%20ottobre%202025_Nazionale%20A%20Femminile.pdf
 |website=[[Italian Football Federation|FIGC]]
 |date=October 2025
 |access-date=8 September 2026
}}</ref>

{{Short description|South Korean politician (born 1990)}} {{Family name hatnote|Shin|lang=Korean}}{{Infobox officeholder|name=Shin Ji-ye|image=Shin_Ji-ye_Marie_Claire.jpg|office=Co-chair of the [[Green Party Korea|Green Party]]|term_start=2018|term_end=2020|alongside=Ha Seung-soo|predecessor=Kim Ju-on and Choi Hyeok-bong|successor=Sung Mi-sun|birth_date={{Birth date and age|1990|06|20}}|native_name=신지예|native_name_lang=ko|party=[[Independent politician|Independent]] (2011–2012; 2020–)|other_party=[[Democratic Labor Party (South Korea)|Democratic Labor Party]] (2011)
[[Green Party Korea|Green Party]] (2012–2020)
[[People Power Party]] (2020–2021){{efn|Joined [[Yoon Suk-yeol]] campaign camp but did not join the party}}}} {{Progressivism in South Korea|People}} '''Shin Ji-ye''' ({{Korean|hangul=신지예}}, born {{Birth date|1990|06|20|df=yes}}) is a [[South Korea|South Korean]] politician.{{Cite web |title=신지예 누구? 역대 최연소 서울시장 후보 출마, 슬로건‘페미니스트 서울시장’ |url=https://www.kookje.co.kr/news2011/asp/newsbody.asp?code=0100&key=20190110.99099004535 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=국제신문}} == Biography == Shin served as leader of the Korea Youth Association from 2004 to 2005.{{Cite web |date=2022-08-18 |title=신지예 나이 고향 학력 이력 프로필 (페미니스트 정치인) |url=https://peoplemoa.co.kr/entry/%EC%8B%A0%EC%A7%80%EC%98%88-%EB%82%98%EC%9D%B4-%EA%B3%A0%ED%96%A5-%ED%95%99%EB%A0%A5-%EC%9D%B4%EB%A0%A5-%ED%94%84%EB%A1%9C%ED%95%84-%ED%8E%98%EB%AF%B8%EB%8B%88%EC%8A%A4%ED%8A%B8-%EC%A0%95%EC%B9%98%EC%9D%B8 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=이것조것 |language=ko}} In 2018, she ran for [[Mayor of Seoul|Seoul Mayor]] as the Green Party candidate in the [[2018 South Korean local elections]].{{Cite web |title=서울특별시 미디어재단 TBS |url=http://tbs.seoul.kr/news/bunya.do?method=daum_html2&typ_800=9&seq_800=10265076 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=tbs.seoul.kr |language=ko}} She adopted "Feminist Mayor" as a slogan and championed the necessity of feminist politics. The campaign garnered significant support while simultaneously facing numerous setbacks, including the repeated defacement of campaign posters.{{Cite web |last=이지영 |date=2018-06-14 |title=‘페미니스트 서울시장 후보’ 녹색당 신지예… 정의당 앞지르며 파란 |url=https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/22715081 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=중앙일보 |language=ko}} Running on a feminist platform, she secured 82,874 votes, finishing fourth (with 1.7% of the vote).{{Cite web |date=2018-06-14 |title=‘페미니즘 정치’ 첫발 뗀 신지예 “이번 선거는 끝이 아닌 시작” |url=https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/politics/assembly/848994.html |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=한겨레 |language=ko}}{{Cite news |last=설승은 |date=2018-06-14 |title=[표] 서울시장 후보별 득표 현황(최종) {{!}} 연합뉴스 |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20180613125151001 |access-date=2026-09-17 |work=연합뉴스 |language=ko-KR}} During the local elections, campaign posters for Candidate Shin were damaged. According to Candidate Shin’s camp on 6 June 2018, a total of 27 posters were defaced after the official campaign period began on 31 May, when the posters were put up: 21 in Gangnam-gu, and one each in Dongdaemun-gu, Nowon-gu, Guro-gu, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seodaemun-gu, and Gangdong-gu.{{Cite web |last=한영혜 |date=2018-06-07 |title=‘페미니스트 서울시장 후보’ 신지예 벽보가 유난히 훼손 많은 이유 |url=https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/22691787 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=중앙일보 |language=ko}} On 22 January 2020, she resigned as co-chair of the [[Green Party Korea|Green Party]].{{Cite web |last=황금비 |date=2020-03-24 |title=[2020총선] 신지예 “민주당을 믿었던 녹색당이 나이브했다” |url=https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/politics/assembly/933948.html |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=한겨레 |language=ko}} Subsequently, she ran as an independent candidate in the [[Seodaemun A]] district, finishing third with 3.23 percent of the vote.{{Cite web |date=2020-05-07 |title='서른 되면 죽자'던 신지예는 다시 창당을 꿈꾼다 |url=https://www.ohmynews.com/NWS_Web/Series/series_premium_pg.aspx?CNTN_CD=A0002638699&SRS_CD=0000012187 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=ohmynews |language=ko}} Also in 2020, Shin went public with the fact that she had been sexually assaulted by a Green Party official. In 2021, the former Green Party official was sentenced to three and a half years in prison and taken into court custody.{{Cite web |title=신지예 대표 성폭행 전 녹색당 당직자 ‘법정 구속’ |url=https://news.kbs.co.kr/news/pc/view/view.do?ncd=5101217 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=KBS 뉴스 |language=ko}} In the [[2021 South Korean by-elections#Mayor of Seoul|2021 Mayor of Seoul by election]], Shin ran as an independent candidate and finished sixth with 18,039 votes.{{Cite web |date=2021-03-28 |title=Minor candidates want their voices to be heard regardless of election result |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/politics/20210328/minor-candidates-want-their-voices-to-be-heard-regardless-of-election-result |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=The Korea Times |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2021-04-10 |title=‘20대 여성들’은 왜 오세훈을 선택하지 않았나?…제3후보 ‘15%’ |url=https://www.donga.com/news/Society/article/all/20210410/106340816/1 |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=동아일보 |language=ko}}{{Cite web |last=Park |first=Hae-ri |date=2021-04-09 |title="왜 1번도 2번도 아니었겠나"…20대女 15%가 찍은 이들의 변 |url=https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/24031862 |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=중앙일보 |language=ko}} === Yoon Suk-yeol presidential campaign === In December 2021, Shin joined the presidential campaign of [[Yoon Suk Yeol|Yoon Suk-yeol]] becoming a senior vice chair of the New Generation Policy Committee. She said she accepted the position because "(Yoon) pledged to resolve violence against women, address the climate crisis and create a Republic of Korea that overcomes (the division of) left and right and moves forward, so I decided to take part."{{Cite web |last=Hyun-su |first=Yim |date=2021-12-21 |title=[Newsmaker] Yoon's feminist recruit under attack from all corners |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/2745168 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}} However, following a reshuffle, she resigned from the campaign in 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-01-03 |title=말 아낀 이준석 "신지예 사퇴에 의견 안 냈다" |url=https://www.ohmynews.com/NWS_Web/View/at_pg.aspx?CNTN_CD=A0002799890 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=오마이뉴스 |language=ko}} == Controversy == A dispute arose with [[Lee Jun-seok]], a Supreme Council member of the [[Bareunmirae Party]], regarding the "Isu Station assault case," which involved a physical altercation between two women and three men. Shin Ji-ye’s side argued that it was a hate crime against women, maintaining that the women were indeed assaulted regardless of whether any verbal abuse had occurred; conversely, Lee Jun-seok contended that the women were the aggressors, as the female group had directed sexual harassment at the men. Regarding the incident, the Dongjak Police Station announced during a briefing on 16 November 2018 that investigations revealed violence had been committed by both parties, noting that it was one of the women who initiated physical contact.{{Cite web |last=기자 |first=노우리 인턴 |date=2020-07-18 |title=신지예·이준석 '이수역 폭행 사건 설전'…"여성 증오 범죄" VS "여성이 가해자" |url=https://www.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2018/11/16/2018111601786.html |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=조선일보 |language=ko}} == Notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} [[Category:21st-century South Korean people]] [[Category:20th-century South Korean people]] [[Category:South Korean women in politics]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1990 births]]

'''Jon Insausti Maisterra''' (born 21 February 1989)<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sainz |first1=Jorge |title=Jon Insausti, una trayectoria fulgurante para llegar a la Alcaldía de San Sebastián|trans-title=Jon Insausti, a dazzling career path to arrive as mayor of San Sebastián|url=https://www.diariovasco.com/san-sebastian/jon-insausti-trayectoria-fulgurante-llegar-alcaldia-20251005232457-nt.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[El Diario Vasco]] |date=5 October 2025 |language=Spanish}}</ref> is a Spanish politician of the [[Basque Nationalist Party]] (EAJ-PNV). He was elected to the city council of [[San Sebastián]] in 2015 and became the mayor in 2025.

==Biography==
Born in [[San Sebastián]], Insausti graduated in business administration from the [[University of the Basque Country]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rodríguez Iñarra |first1=Nerea |title=Jon Insausti sustituye a Eneko Goia en la alcaldía de San Sebastián|trans-title=Jon Insausti replaces Eneko Goia as mayor of San Sebastián |url=https://cadenaser.com/euskadi/2025/10/02/jon-insausti-es-el-nuevo-alcalde-de-donostia-tras-su-etapa-como-concejal-de-cultura-euskera-y-turismo-radio-san-sebastian/ |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=[[Cadena SER]] |date=2 October 2025 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He was elected to the city council in 2015, with [[Eneko Goia]] of his party becoming mayor, and in January 2018 he was put in charge of culture and education, as well as being made spokesperson of the party group.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jon Insausti releva a Miren Azkarate como concejal de Cultura y Educación|trans-title=Jon Insausti replaces Miren Azkarate as councillor for Cultrue and Education
 |url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2018/01/26/radio_san_sebastian/1516984849_606036.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=[[Cadena SER]] |date=26 January 2018 |language=Spanish}}</ref> For the [[2019 Spanish local elections]] he was put eighth on the party list,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Muñoz |first1=Ainhoa |title=Goia sitúa a Nekane Arzallus como número dos por su experiencia urbanística|trans-title=Goia puts Nekane Arzallus as number two for her city planning experience|url=https://www.diariovasco.com/politica/goia-situa-nekane-20190126004306-ntvo.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[El Diario Vasco]] |date=26 January 2019 |language=Spanish}}</ref> and ten were elected.<ref>{{cite news |title=El PNV gana en San Sebastián y suma un edil más|trans-title=PNV win in San Sebastián and add one more councillor |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/elecciones/forales-municipales/supera-cuatro-escanos-20190526220941-nt.html|access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[El Correo]] |date=26 May 2019 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He was put in charge of culture and the [[Basque language]], and for the [[2023 Spanish local elections|2023 elections]] he was placed third,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Aresti |first1=E. |title=El PNV aprueba su lista para las municipales de Donostia|trans-title=PNV approves its list for the municipal elections in San Sebastián |url=https://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.eus/politica/2023/02/28/pnv-aprueba-lista-municipales-donostia-6509084.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=Noticias de Gipuzkoa |date=23 February 2023 |language=Spanish}}</ref> as his party took nine seats.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Astarloa |first1=Iraitz |title=Estos son los concejales del Ayuntamiento de Donostia|trans-title=These are the councillors of San Sebastián City Council |url=https://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.eus/fotos/2023/05/28/concejales-ayuntamiento-donostia-6846113.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=Noticias de Gipuzkoa |date=17 June 2023 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

On 2 October 2025, Goia resigned after a decade as mayor and said that his successor would be appointed by the party leadership, amid speculation that it would be Insausti.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Díaz |first1=Martxelo |title=Eneko Goia deja la Alcaldía de Donostia el día 16 tras diez años en el cargo|trans-title=Eneko Goia steps down as mayor San Sebastián on 16 October after ten years in the role|url=https://www.naiz.eus/en/info/noticia/20251002/eneko-goia-deja-la-alcaldia-de-donostia-tras-10-anos-en-el-cargo |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=Naiz |date=2 October 2026 |language=Spanish}}</ref> The following day, Insausti was confirmed as successor, with the handover planned for Goia's resignation date of 16 October.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rioja Andueza |first1=Iker |title=El PNV presenta a Jon Insausti como nuevo alcalde de Donostia, “un relevo con naturalidad y buena armonía”|trans-title=PNV presents Jon Insausti as new mayor of San Sebastián, "a natural replacement with good harmony"|url=https://www.eldiario.es/euskadi/pnv-presenta-jon-insausti-nuevo-alcalde-donostia-relevo-naturalidad-buena-armonia_1_12653415.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[elDiario.es]] |date=3 October 2025 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He was invested as mayor on 29 October.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bilbao |first1=Usua |title=Jon Insausti se convierte en el nuevo alcalde de San Sebastián y marca el rumbo para "transformar la ciudad"|trans-title=Jon Insausti becomes the new mayor of San Sebastián and sets course to "transform the city"|url=https://www.cope.es/emisoras/pais-vasco/guipuzcoa/san-sebastian/noticias/jon-insausti-convierte-nuevo-alcalde-san-sebastian-marca-rumbo-transformar-ciudad-20251029_3241549.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |publisher=[[Cadena COPE]] |date=29 October 2025 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

As mayor, Insausti opposed holiday let apartments. After a 2018 regulation, their number dropped from 2,200 to 1,300, or 1.4% of the city, which he considered still too high. In April 2025, while in charge of tourism, he said that the greater problem for housing was second homes and vacant properties, which were 16% of residences.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mata |first1=Miguel Ángel |last2=Villameriel |first2=Miguel |title=Donostia y Bilbao abogan por «apretar más» a los pisos turísticos para sacar vivienda al mercado|trans-title=San Sebastián and Bilbao advocate for "tightening the screws" on tourist apartments to bring housing onto the market|url=https://www.diariovasco.com/gipuzkoa/insausti-pisos-turisticos-licencias-20251119124920-nt.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[El Diario Vasco]] |date=19 November 2025 |language=Spanish}}</ref> In July 2026, a tourist tax was approved, which was projected to make €8 million annually.<ref>{{cite news |title=San Sebastián aprueba una tasa turística con un tope de seis noches: estas son las tarifas propuestas para quien visite la ciudad|trans-title=San Sebastián approves a tourist tax with a limit of six nights: these are the proposed rates for visitors to the city |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.es/life/viajes/san-sebastian-aprueba-tasa-turistica-tope-seis-noches-son-tarifas-propuesta-visite-ciudad-f202607.html |access-date=5 October 2026 |work=[[HuffPost]] |agency=[[EFE]] |date=28 July 2026 |language=Spanish}}</ref>
